scoring_rubric.2: Present and extractable — explicitly stated on page, not linked or implied
scoring_rubric.1: Partial — incomplete, vague, or only linked to another page
scoring_rubric.0: Absent — nothing on page addresses this question
scoring_rubric.unclear_extraction_failure: Page too thin or navigation-heavy to evaluate
scoring_rubric.unclear_content_behind_barrier: Information likely exists behind login or form
scoring_rubric.unclear_ambiguous_reference: Something relevant present but cannot be scored confidently

pages.evaluator_notes: Edge case page. Q8 is the hardest scoring call in the set — exhaustive course lists for all three emphases with course numbers and titles. Agent must recognize content-rich non-standard presentation and score 2, not default to 1 because there is no clean summary table. Q9 partial is a subtle call — acclaimed faculty and award-winning creative writers mentioned but no names given. Cross-page coherence note: this page and the BBA page use the same general template but have vastly different content quality — same template, 11 vs 15 score.

pages.page_title: Air and Space Law Graduate Certificate
pages.evaluator_notes: Worst page in the set. Degree field in Program Information box is blank — template designed for degree programs cannot represent a certificate program, resulting in empty field rather than N/A or Graduate Certificate. This is a CMS template mismatch, not missing content — the finding routes to IT not the content team. Apply Now button links to LSAC.org external service, not Ole Miss directly — broken user journey. No prerequisites stated despite this being a graduate certificate explicitly targeting legal professionals and policymakers — a prospective student cannot determine if they are eligible. Audience mismatch with all other pages — this is graduate/professional, not undergraduate.

cross_page_notes.finding: Accountancy page uses BLS as salary data source. Social Work page uses Indeed for some figures and BLS for others. Same institution, different data source standards — cross-page coherence finding.

BBA and English pages use the same general template. BBA scores 11/24, English scores 15/24. Same structure, vastly different content investment — institutional content quality differential worth surfacing.
Q11 (what happens after I apply) scores 0 on four of five pages and 1 on one page. Universal gap across the institution — no program page explains the post-application process.
Q1 (cost) scores 1 on all five pages. Every page links to cost information but none states a cost figure directly. Institutional-level pattern, not individual page failure.

Certificate program uses degree program template resulting in blank Degree field. Finding routes to IT/CMS team not content team. Likely affects other certificate and specialist programs across the institution.
